name: Cessna 180/185 Skywagon
summary: Rugged tailwheel four-to-six-seat high-wing utility singles, the classic bush and floatplane Cessnas of Alaska and the backcountry.

wings: High wing braced by a single lift strut per side
Constant-chord inner section with tapered outer panels
engines: Six-cylinder engine in a deep cowling
fuselage: Conventional tailwheel gear with spring-steel main legs
All-metal four-to-six-seat cabin sitting nose-high on the ground
Frequently on floats, skis or oversized tundra tires
tail: Rounded straight fin on early 180s; taller squared fin with dorsal fillet on later 180s and the 185

tellTales: All-metal strut-braced high-wing four-seater on a tailwheel
Deep nose cowl — a heavy airplane, not a light two-seat taildragger
Often on floats or big bush tires

confusedWith.howToTell: The 180/185 is a taildragger; the 182 has tricycle gear.
The Maule has a fabric-covered tube fuselage, a swept square-topped fin and a short stubby nose; the 180/185 is all-metal with a smoothly tapered rear fuselage.
The Beaver is larger with a round radial-engine cowl and a boxy fuselage; the 180/185 has a flat-engine cowl.
The 180 seats four side-by-side with one rear window; the Bird Dog seats two in tandem under an enormous glazed rear cabin.
The 180 has a bigger cowl, a taller swept fin and more cabin glazing; the 170 is smaller with a slimmer cowl and a smaller fin.
The 180 has a flat engine in a slimmer cowl and a lift strut; the 195 has a big radial engine in a round cowl and no wing struts.
